newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nippon Oil's six-month current profits plunge.
newsitem.headline: Nippon Oil's six-month current profits plunge.

text.p: Nippon Oil Co Ltd said on Wednesday that its parent current profit for the six months to September totaled 946 million yen, down 86.8 percent, or about 6.3 billion yen, from the same period a year earlier.
The leading oil refiner said sales for the April-September period rose nine percent to 867.7 billion yen. It forecast current profits of 12 billion yen for fiscal 1996/97.

Nippon Oil managing director Yusuke Ishimura said the current profit decline could be attributed to a number of factors, including the impact of a new wholesale price system introduced in April in anticipation of market liberalisation.
Japanese refiners introduced a new wholesale price system which brings kerosene and gas oil prices higher while lowering the price of gasoline, previously a pillar of their income.
However, while gasoline retail prices have fallen, there has not been a matching rise in retail prices of kerosene and gas oil, and this has depressed company profits, Ishimura said.
He also blamed a rise in crude oil prices this year and the weaker yen.
He said there was a time lag before the effects of higher crude oil prices and the lower yen could be passed on to sales prices.
Anticipating a decline in profits, Japanese oil refiners have been taking steps to streamline and cut costs, Ishimura said.
Nippon Oil has cut costs by 4.3 billion yen for the six-month period to September in areas such as distribution and personnel.
"We expected profits to decline...and we have taken steps to cut costs," Ishimura said.
He said Nippon Oil -- which did not hire any college graduates this year -- has decided to refrain from hiring any graduates in 1997 as well.
